text.p: Following are the main stories in Friday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Leaders of the United Malays National Organisation and the splinter party, Parti Melayu Semangat 46, today held hands and, in a public declaration of reconciliation, spoke of a common theme -- unity.
- Gerakan party president Lim Keng Yaik has agreed to meet Batu member of parliament Joseph Chong at the party headquarters tomorrow. Chong is challenging Lim for the leadership of the party.
- Motosikal dan Engin Nasional Sdn Bhd (Modenas), manufacturer of the Malaysian-made motorcycle named Kriss by Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad yesterday, hopes to break even in five years.

- Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad yesterday reiterated his call to fundamentalist Parti Islam Se-Malaysia (PAS) leaders and members to emulate splinter party Parti Melayu Semangat 46 and join the United Malays National Organisation to make Muslim unity more meaningful.
- The Lion Group is no longer involved in the proposed rescue of financially-troubled steelmaker Perwaja Steel Sdn Bhd.
- Malaysia can no longer be overdependent on foreign labour as social problems created by foreign workers are already taking a toll, Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad said.
